fix(facts): one transcript fold in flight per session; the gate places every built-in, can snapshot its heap, and is re-priced for it (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.c0y) (#622)

* fix(facts): one transcript fold in flight per session; the gate places every built-in and can snapshot its heap (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.c0y)

The 100-session gate failed with metrics and activity on because the
transcript fold started a new fold for every request of a session while
the session's first fold was still out, and a cold fold re-enters the
8-slot read gate once per window: folds arrived faster than any could
finish, none landed, the stamp fast path never engaged, and every
request's refresh stayed alive in the queue. The fold now coalesces per
session through the same SingleFlight the usage store's request refresh
uses.

The gate's config places metrics, activity, tokenSparkline and
autocompact, so it gathers every built-in the facts epic makes
always-on. `--heap-snapshots DIR` has the daemon write its heap at the
two collections through Node's signal snapshot; the whole-file wait
moves from capture-heap into scripts/lib and both call it.

* fix(load-gate): re-derive the budget from CI with every built-in placed (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.c0y)

Measured on PR #622's CI: 186 MB charged once collected at 20 sessions (feed criterion, feed off) and 514 MB at 100 (load gate). per-session = (514 - 186) / 80 = 4.1 MB, base = 186 - 20 * 4.1 = 104 MB, headroom a fifth as before. The gate placed neither metrics nor activity when the old 112 + 3.1 MB were measured.

* fix(scripts): a snapshot is matched by V8's name shape, the wait reuses sleep, NODE_OPTIONS is quoted; the fold's key comment says why the stamp is left out (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.c0y)

* fix(load-gate): the budget check is unjudged under snapshots; the snapshot wait and NODE_OPTIONS form live in the lib; the fold's memory line states a consequence (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.c0y)

fix(home): a misstated home is refused where the world is built; the socket file takes a parsed name; the help and README name the home

Review (second high): the one-line refusal lived in the CLI entry alone, so the demo, the gallery and the load gate printed a stack trace for the same input. The socket-file rule took any string though only main's name or a parsed name can reach it. The usage bench built three worlds per sampled store. The design doc's breaker line and the user-facing help, README and authoring doc now say what the code does.

fix(home): a main renderer's child parses main's roots; the entry refuses a misstated home in one line; the suite drops an inherited socket override

Review (medium): the environment a main renderer hands a child carried its socket but not its XDG roots, so a child under the tmux server's environment derived another state and config tree. The entry built its world at module top level, so a half-set home printed a stack trace where the Rust client prints one line. Every Jest worker is a named home, which refuses the legacy socket override beside it, so a shell exporting it refused the whole suite. The socket directory's ownership check reads the uid as the runtime directory's name does. Three design docs named the override as the knob.

fix(home): the tmux row carries the renderer's own name; a relative runtime directory is refused in both runtimes; the bench reaches main's home

Review (high): the tmux status line stamped every row `main` though the daemon holds its home's name. The runtime-directory override was accepted relative while the root was refused for the same reason. The uid is read from the kernel, as the Rust client reads it. The click bench stripped only the legacy socket variable to reach the default socket; it drops every home variable now. The effects-at-boundaries marker the rewrite dropped from the state derivation is restored, and the breaker's and the contracts table's stale naming of the legacy variable is replaced.
test(home): finish the rebase over main's load-config removal and in-turn click context

test(home): a test's repo answers and main-layout environment follow its own host

The worker is a named home, so a test that builds a main home over the
worker's environment reads a state directory the repo-approval helper did
not write to by default; every such test now answers through its own host.
The main-layout environment is read when asked, as the live process
environment is, so a PATH of stubs written before the host is built reaches
the launcher's children. The e2e click stand-in makes the state directory
the daemon it plays would. The CLI probe test reaches the isolated daemon
through a world over its own home. The node_modules symlink a worktree
carries is untracked, and ignored by name rather than as a directory.

fix(load-gate): the steady phase begins once the daemon has settled, a wait with no time left takes no loop turn, and a failed render names what the daemon's log shows over it (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.09c)

The one failed render of run 42154313711 was not a GC pause: the daemon logged a line every 10-34 ms through the episode. It was a saturated loop while the speed lane was still landing for every session, 13 s into a steady phase that had begun before the daemon settled, and the failed request lost its last 54 ms to a 0 ms timer behind the poll phase. The gate now waits for every session's latest render to be answered inside its wait, at both points the steady phase must not inherit a backlog from; waitWithin with no time left aborts in the same turn; each steady failure carries the daemon's lines, longest silence and deadline draws over its round trip, and the facts carry the connect-to-wait spread.

feat(apply): a request takes its turn; its two writes are one batch in the request arm, and the answered mark is an event (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.1ql)

The request arm records what the client said (client-hints, render-origin)
as one setBatch inside a journal turn and draws once the turn is over, so a
request that arrives while a click's turn is held draws the click whole,
never its first write beside the request's hints. The turn waits behind
turns alone: a click's head gather holds none. The click error's answered
mark, the one other request-path write, is an `answered` event whose arm
takes a turn; the delivery edge applies it as the performer applies
effect-done, with a refusal said in the log.

The render line gains renderer=main, factsSeq, turnWait and revision; the
request's apply line stays null, since the render event is its one record.
The daemon's draw is a port on the request arm's parts, so the arm is
driven below the daemon. The daemon's adapters gain `sessionWrites`: the
production daemon writes the store, every daemon built in a worker writes
through the write-outside-turn instrument. A run's ending and a lane
setup's failure still write the store outside a turn (the next story).

Tests: test/request-turn.test.ts races a request against a click whose
doctor gathers inside its turn under a held clock, and against one parked
in its head gather; apply-effects covers the answered mark's turn. The
boot ratchet forbids a new in-worker case, so the race lives at the root
over Apply and the real journal turns.

chore(facts): delete the wants closure (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.xb3)

The facts document is total, so the question "which fields does this config
read" has no caller with a reason. Every session now gathers every built-in:
git runs one constant option set (forge lookup included), every declared
plugin source is held, and burn, block and autocompact's context cap are always
composed. A view's declaration depends on the request alone, so a preset pick
moves no hold.

Deleted: the wants function, the needed-prefix builders, the sources-read walk,
the closure parameter through declare/refresh/read/project, the PR reads gate,
the git options derived from the closure, `Gathered`, `declaredSources`, and the
view's preset reaction. The doctor's data-needs walk stays and now owns its own
per-segment path closure, since it answers what a config would read.

The bar is byte-identical; the payload golden gains the keys that were gated
(block, burn, metrics, activity, tmux and the like on presets that did not read
them). Tests that asserted gating are deleted; the fold-edge cases they covered
(partials, helpers handed a dict) move to the doctor's path closure.
